title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 31 (“Contingent contract” defined)

content.overview: Section 31 provides that a “contingent contract” is a contract to do or not to do something, if some event, collateral to such contract, does or does not happen.
content.glance: Contingent contract = performance depends on a collateral uncertain event happening or not happening.
content.study: A contingent contract is a contract to do or not to do something if some event collateral to the contract does or does not happen. Enforcement rules are in ss. 32–36. Distinguish from wagers (s. 30). Current-law framing: identify the collateral event; classify as contingent; apply ss. 32–36 for enforcement or voidness.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: Contract to do or not to do something if some event collateral to such contract does or does not happen.

examples.title: Insurance
examples.body: A contracts to pay B a sum if B’s house is burnt. That is a contingent contract under s. 31.

hypotheticals.question: Is every contract depending on an uncertain event a wager?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Contingent contracts (s. 31) may be valid; wagers are void under s. 30.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-31
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Contingent contracts are the same as wagers.
misconceptions.correction: Contingent contracts may be enforceable; wagers under s. 30 are void.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 31 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify collateral event. II. Classify as contingent contract. III. Apply ss. 32–36. IV. Distinguish s. 30. V. Conclude.
